newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down on continued political crux.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down on continued political crux.

text.p: Thai stocks moved in the negative zone throughout the session on Wednesday and closed slightly lower as investors grew weary over a delay in the nomination of a new premier, brokers said.
The SET index ended 7.27 points lower at 1,034.94 on 3.3 billion baht trade. Decliners led gainers 225 to 91 while 100 issues were unchanged. The SET-50 index was 0.69 point down to 78.97.
"Investors sold stocks after they felt it was taking too long to nominate the new prime minister. They're getting a bit frustrated," said Sanpong Limthamrongkul of Jardine Fleming.
Brokers said investors felt uncertain as long as the nomination of the new prime minister was not settled.
The nomination of a new premier would give a clearer picture to investors on who would be appointed to key economic ministerial portfolios, brokers said.

The market initially rose after Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa announced on Saturday he was stepping down in seven days. Leaders of the six-party coalition are currently discussing who would succeed Banharn.
The finance sector fell most due to profit taking, slipping 2.24 percent. The banking sector was down 0.97 percent and the property sector declined 0.47 percent.

Debuting stock GCN Finance topped the lists of most active stocks in terms of value and volume, ending down 3.25 baht from its initial public offering price of 28 baht. Finance One fell 2.50 to 99.50 while Bangkok Bank slipped two to 216 and Italian-Thai Development declined two to 173.
Brokers said the index is expected to continue falling on Thursday as investors continue to wait for the nomination of the new prime minister. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
